title: Humpback Whales Trap Fish in a 98-Foot Net Made of Bubbles

scenes.text: Humpback whales trap fish inside a net made of bubbles.
One whale swims in a circle, blowing bubbles from its blowhole.
The bubbles form a net up to 98 feet wide that fish avoid.
Up to twenty whales feed together while the fish stay trapped in the middle.
Then they rise through the net with mouths wide open, taking in up to 15,000 gallons of water.
The net lasts only a couple of minutes. A net made of nothing but bubbles.

description:
Humpback whales trap fish inside a net made of bubbles up to 98 feet wide.
Then they swim up through it with mouths open, gulping up to 15,000 gallons of water.
Would you believe a net can be made of air?
